pull:
A man broke into your box to leave you a list with your name on it.

**One day north: the Hollow Wake Inn. Somebody wants you there.**
forkA: The list is a warning.
forkB: The list is an invitation.

leads.place: the list, by the last light

actions.verb: read it again, line by line
hold it to the light and look at the ink

leads.clueText: Not one name is crossed out or written over. Every line sits level, and the inn's line is in the same hand as the names.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

leads.place: the trees where he went

actions.verb: go after him into the trees
pick out his trail in the dusk

leads.clueText: Twenty paces in, his prints meet another man's. The two go on together, at a walk.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

leads.place: the bottom of the cargo box

actions.verb: take the box apart, board by board
go through it a third time

leads.clueText: Under your things lies a square of oilcloth you never packed, folded small. Whatever he put in the box, he wrapped it first against the wet.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

nudge: {friend:Intellect}, what is odd about a stranger who leaves something behind?
opener: One list, one inn's name. Nothing was taken.
weekQuestion: Why are our names on that list?
meaningQuestion: *"One stayed close."* Close to what?

pull: **First light. Two hours north. A child was held at that rock, and whatever it is has not finished.**
forkA: Meira left in a hurry.
forkB: Meira left on purpose.

leads.place: the bottom of her satchel

actions.verb: empty it out onto the table
feel along the lining

leads.clueText: In the bottom of the satchel: a heel of bread in a cloth, hard as wood, and a new candle that was never lit.
leads.lateLine: You almost give up. Then, at the last of the light, there it is.

leads.place: the notebook, page by page

actions.verb: go through it, leaf by leaf
look at how each page is kept

leads.clueText: Every loose slip in the notebook is pinned to the page it belongs with. Not one is out of place.
leads.lateLine: You almost give up. Then, at the last of the light, there it is.

leads.place: the seat that was hers

actions.verb: sit where she sat and look out
go from her seat to the nearest door

leads.clueText: Her seat is the end of a bench. It is worn pale on one side only: the side nearer the door.
leads.lateLine: You almost give up. Then, at the last of the light, there it is.

nudge: {friend:Craft}, how would you test whether the page is hers?
opener: You've paid for your rooms and you haven't burned anything down. That's more than most guests manage.

riddle.q: What has a neck but no head?
riddle.quip: The inn is full of them. None of them talk.

callback: She hasn't sat in that seat for three weeks. Your pages all reached you on the road within the same few days.
weekQuestion: Why are our names on that list?
meaningQuestion: *"They wept for him before they feared him."* What changed between the two?

pull:
Garrick has not gone back to his inn. He is standing in the road with his pack on, looking at the smoke.

**The ruts go that way. So did the man. He will be there before you, and every door will be shut when you come.**
forkA: The man in the bracken was guarding the rock.
forkB: He was waiting for us.

leads.place: the bracken where he waited

actions.verb: crawl into his hollow in the bracken
read the ground he lay on

leads.clueText: In the flattened bracken a flask has left a ring in the dew, and a second ring beside it where he set it down again.
leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

leads.place: the far side of the rock

actions.verb: climb round the split to the far side
pace out the ground round its foot

leads.clueText: Round the foot of the rock the turf is worn to bare earth in a narrow path, all the way round. Someone walks round this stone, and often.
leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

leads.place: the gap he ran through

actions.verb: run his line to the trees
search the ground he crossed

leads.clueText: In the gap where he ran, a stick lies dropped, notched down one side. The newest notches are still pale and wet.
leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

nudge: {friend:Aim}, from his hollow in the bracken, what was he watching?
opener: You've not eaten. Sit.

riddle.q: The more you take, the more you leave behind. What am I?
riddle.quip: There's bracken full of them out there.

callback: The man on the forest road was carrying her rubbing. The man in the bracken was watching her rock.
weekQuestion: Why are our names on that list?
meaningQuestion: *"Some locks already know their key."* Whose key?

pull: **East. Two hours. He has half a day on you, and he is heading for the only other person alive who has seen that knife.**
forkA: The village is protecting the girl.
forkB: The village is protecting itself.

leads.place: the gate at the end of the lane

actions.verb: look at how the gate was left
lift the bar and feel its weight

leads.clueText: The gate at the end of the lane is swinging, but its bar has been lifted and leaned neatly against the post, not thrown down.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

leads.place: the one open shutter

actions.verb: stop at the open shutter and wait
look in from across the lane

leads.clueText: On the sill of the open shutter stands a cup of milk with a cloth over it. Under the window, a child's stool is set square to the wall.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

leads.place: where the elder's men stood

actions.verb: look over the ground where they stood
pick through what they left in the mud

leads.clueText: Where the men stood with the elder, curls of fresh bark lie in the mud. Somebody in Fenmark cut a cudgel today.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

nudge: {friend:Charm}, when Fenmark shut its doors on us, who was it protecting?
opener: A village that won't talk is still talking. Mostly with its shutters.

riddle.q: What breaks the moment you say its name?

callback: The boy says they moved like they'd done it before. The little horse at the rock had sat out a winter or two.
weekQuestion: Why are our names on that list?
meaningQuestion: *"Marked before the first cry's through."* Marked by whom, and for what?

pull:
At first light she walks you to the edge of the camp, and stands on the old charcoal road, and points.

**North. The same man, the same country, the same season. If it comes round like a calendar, the time is now.**
forkA: It's the same man, twice.
forkB: It's a way of working, not one man.

leads.place: the woman at the edge of the firelight

actions.verb: sit with her and let her talk
ask her what she saw two winters back

leads.clueText: She says she never saw his face, only the knife, and it is the knife she knows him by.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

leads.place: the shutter he was trying

actions.verb: run a thumb along the marks in the wood
set the old marks beside the new

leads.clueText: Under his fresh marks on the shutter are older ones, grey with weather, worked in at the same place, where the bar sits.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

leads.place: the clean path in

actions.verb: read the path by the firelight
count the prints worn into it

leads.clueText: The path in is worn by one pair of small boots, hers, over and over. Under them you find no other prints but tonight's.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

nudge: {friend:Intellect}, two children, two winters apart. One man's habit, or someone's way of working?
opener: Two winters between two children. Some people count in winters. It's a way of keeping still.

riddle.q: I grow, but I'm not alive. I need air, but I have no lungs. Water kills me. What am I?
riddle.quip: Which is why I tend this one myself.

callback: The road, the rock, and tonight her shutters. Not one of those men has said a word.
weekQuestion: Why are our names on that list?
meaningQuestion: *"The power that gives is also the power that takes."* What has been given this week, and what has been taken?

pull: **Cross at first light. You will be there by morning. Whatever is at the place the map marks, the season for it is now.**
forkA: They carried her across the water.
forkB: They wanted us to think so.

leads.place: the far bank, along the water

actions.verb: scan the far bank from the ford-stone
wade the safe line across

leads.clueText: On a thorn at the water's edge of the far bank, a little way along from the ruts, a few woollen threads hang at the height of a child.
leads.lateLine: You almost give up. Then, at the last of the light, there it is.

leads.place: the ruts up the far bank

actions.verb: read the hoofprints beside the ruts
cross and walk the ruts up the bank

leads.clueText: Beside the ruts, the horse's prints up the far bank are short, deep and dug in at the toe. It went up at a run.
leads.lateLine: You almost give up. Then, at the last of the light, there it is.

leads.place: the heel-marks at the water

actions.verb: get down to them before the river does
work out whose feet went where

leads.clueText: Beside the heel-marks, a second man's prints come down from the cart to the water and go straight back up to it.
leads.lateLine: You almost give up. Then, at the last of the light, there it is.

nudge: {friend:Intellect}, what do you notice about how the pieces settled?
opener: Six pieces, one map. Eat something before you stare at it.

riddle.q: I have a bed but never sleep, a mouth but never speak. What am I?
riddle.quip: The one in front of us says nothing, and I believe it.

callback: Meira had this shape on paper before any of you found a piece. Tonight the pieces drew it.
weekQuestion: Why are our names on that list?
meaningQuestion: *"The key that locks."* What is locked, and who holds the key?

pull: **The mill is an hour on. At first light: what did the family see?**
forkA: They're keeping Corin close, upriver.
forkB: Upriver is only the road away.

leads.place: the bench by his door

actions.verb: let him tell it his own way
ask him about the horse, not the men

leads.clueText: The old man says the horse never balked at his gate or at the fork, in full dark and with no lamp. It took the mill lane at a steady walk.
leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

leads.place: the fresh ruts in the lane

actions.verb: follow the ruts past his gate
read where the wheels ran

leads.clueText: The ruts run past his gate without a check. By that gate, in plain sight of the lane, a child's wooden horse lies on its side in the grass.
leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

leads.place: where the cart turned upriver

actions.verb: run down to the turn before dark
read the turn in the half-light

leads.clueText: Where the cart turned upriver, the ruts coming down sink deeper into the verge than the ruts going up.
leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

nudge: {friend:Aim}, the cart turned upriver. How far do you think it went?
place: The mine, then the mill road
opener: Beds are in the barn tonight. Pick a corner and take it.

riddle.q: I have a face and two hands but no arms or legs. What am I?
riddle.quip: Time's the one thing the cart has on us.

callback: The mine wall put Tamsin's name first and Corin's second. Tamsin heard them say "the mill boy next".
weekQuestion: Why these children, and not any others?
meaningQuestion: *"We held his last wall."* Whose wall, and why was it meant to fall?

pull: **Upriver. The ruts are four nights old, and there is weather coming.**
forkA: They had a list with birthdays.
forkB: They knew him personally.

leads.place: the doorway, with her

actions.verb: ask her what was in his hands
ask her what he did before he spoke

leads.clueText: She says he had a folded paper in his fist. He looked at it once, then said the boy's name.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

leads.place: inside the mill door

actions.verb: follow his boot-marks inside
read the dried mud on the boards

leads.clueText: Nobody has swept since. His dried boot-mud goes from the door straight to the boy's bed and back, and never turns aside.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

leads.place: the yard where the cart stood

actions.verb: walk the yard by the light from the door
read what the horse left behind

leads.clueText: Where the cart stood in the yard, the grass is cropped short in a wide half-circle, as far as a tethered horse can reach.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

nudge: {friend:Craft}, how was the mark cut, and with what tool?
opener: Asked for by name, and by the night he was born. That's an odd thing to ask for.

riddle.q: I have teeth but cannot bite. What am I?

callback: In the mine, that shape was a hole, and what sat in it was gone. Here it's cut into the mill's footing.
weekQuestion: Why these children, and not any others?
meaningQuestion: *"By the third, we had stopped."* Why stop counting?

pull: **Where was he trying to get to? The path goes on past him, and up.**
forkA: The stranger wanted the same door.
forkB: The stranger was left as a warning.

leads.place: the stone round the housing

actions.verb: look at the stone round the lock
read the marks cut into it

leads.clueText: The stone round the housing is scored with dozens of short scratches, some weathered and some bright. He tried it more than once, on more than one day.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

leads.place: the stranger on the path

actions.verb: kneel by him and close his eyes
go through what he carried

leads.clueText: His purse is still on his belt, and there is silver in it. A week of people have stepped over him, and not one has taken it.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

leads.place: the narrows where the dog lies

actions.verb: hold the chain short and get past
look past the dog from the rocks

leads.clueText: Behind the dog, at the end of its chain, stands a pail of water, full and clean. There is a scrap of fresh meat beside it.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

nudge: {friend:Intellect}, did that stranger die trying the lock, or was he left for us?
opener: A stranger dead at a lock, and a lock that opened for you. Rooms like that have opinions.

riddle.q: What has many keys but opens no door?
riddle.quip: Not like that lock. It opened for you.

callback: Corin was asked for by name. Today a lock that wouldn't open for a dead man opened for you.
weekQuestion: Why these children, and not any others?
meaningQuestion: *"Ours was the last light burning."* The last of what?

pull: **Is there another way into this hill, before they finish? You have tonight to find it.**
forkA: Now they'll hurry.
forkB: They won't change a thing for us.

leads.place: the foot of the shaft

actions.verb: look down past the edge
creep back to the lip and look

leads.clueText: A second lamp stands lit at the foot of the shaft, filled and trimmed, the same make as the ring in the chamber. Nobody grabbed it in a hurry.
leads.lateLine: You almost give up. Then, at the last of the light, there it is.

leads.place: the timbers at the shaft's mouth

actions.verb: look over the timbering at the top
follow the timber down by the lamplight

leads.clueText: On the timbering just below the top, a fresh pale scar runs down the wood, where a stone knocked loose went bouncing all the way to the bottom.
leads.lateLine: You almost give up. Then, at the last of the light, there it is.

leads.place: the voices down the shaft

actions.verb: lie flat at the edge and listen
count the voices as they go round

leads.clueText: When the shout went up, the heads turned, but the chant never stopped. It ran on under the shout the whole time, the same few words.
leads.lateLine: You almost give up. Then, at the last of the light, there it is.

nudge: {friend:Charm}, the voices below all said the same words. What were they getting ready?
opener: Sit down before you fall down.

riddle.q: What can fill a cave and weigh nothing?

callback: Yesterday a branch swung on the slope with no wind. Today they knew you were at the shaft.
weekQuestion: Why these children, and not any others?
meaningQuestion: *"His hand was bleeding, and he told us to sleep."* What did he do down there?

pull: **There is no second door on this hillside, and now there is a clock. Last week, six cold slivers showed you a way nobody was watching. You have five.**
forkA: The king was erased by his enemies.
forkB: The king was erased by his own people.

leads.place: the old stone where he signalled

actions.verb: run a hand over each face of it
look at it side-on by the lamp

leads.clueText: On the old stone where the scout stood, one face has been ground flat, long ago. The chisel scars are weathered grey. Whatever was carved there is gone.
leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

leads.place: the scree below the stone

actions.verb: scramble down the scree
search the scree by lamplight

leads.clueText: Mixed into the scree are chips of dressed stone, blackened by fire. One still carries the curve of a carved letter, broken off mid-word.
leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

leads.place: the fallen sheepfold

actions.verb: lift the fallen stones one by one
look at how the fold was built

leads.clueText: The fold's old cut stones were laid with their carved sides turned inward, against each other, every one. From outside, the wall shows nothing.
leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

nudge: {friend:Intellect}, who gains from a forgotten name?
opener: A small black circle. Somebody wanted a thing forgotten, and somebody else wouldn't let it be.

riddle.q: What has no beginning, no middle and no end?
riddle.quip: A small black one, this evening.

callback: On Day 2 a horn button, on Day 3 a dead stranger. Tonight, a circle.
weekQuestion: Why these children, and not any others?
meaningQuestion: *"Not one of us who would not have died for him."* Who was he, to the people who wrote this?

pull: **They are digging toward the old room. Be in it first.**
forkA: They're digging toward the old room to get in.
forkB: They're digging to find something that's already there.

leads.place: the ground over the picks

actions.verb: feel the strokes through the turf
time the strokes and place them

leads.clueText: The strokes come from one place only, and each new stroke lands a little nearer the old shaft than the last.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

leads.place: the two lamps at the foot

actions.verb: watch what passes the lamps
crawl to the edge and look down

leads.clueText: In the lamplight at the foot of the shaft, baskets of dug earth are tipped out. Someone kneels and sifts each one through their hands before it is thrown aside.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

leads.place: the hole under the old stone

actions.verb: shift one more stone
squeeze in to the first step

leads.clueText: Under the stones, the first step down is thick with dust. In the dust there is no print but your own.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

nudge: {friend:Might}, you've heard them digging. Cutting a way in, or searching for something?
opener: Digging toward an older room. You have to respect the effort.

riddle.q: I have rivers with no water and cities with no houses. What am I?

callback: In the mine, you reached the mark after it was emptied. Tonight they're still digging toward the older room.
weekQuestion: Why these children, and not any others?
meaningQuestion: *"Morning came. The enemy did not."* Where did they go?

pull:
They are not hiding her. They told her she was going home.

**Why would anyone take a stolen child back to where she was born? Ashcombe: a long day west.**
forkA: They need her at home.
forkB: Home is only the first stop.

leads.place: Corin, on the walk down

actions.verb: walk beside him and let him talk
look him over in the morning light

leads.clueText: Corin has a child's woollen mitten tucked in his belt that is not his. The wool is rough and grey, and it smells of sheep.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

leads.place: where the cart stood, below the shaft

actions.verb: read what the cart left in the grass
work out what they loaded

leads.clueText: Where the cart stood, a cask has pressed a deep ring into the mud. The grass round it is soaked where they topped it up from the stream, right to the brim.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

leads.place: the shoulder of the hill he ran over

actions.verb: go up the shoulder after him
follow his line from the shaft mouth

leads.clueText: At the top of the shoulder the ground is scuffed where he stood a while, facing west. Then his prints go on, the same way the cart went.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

nudge: {friend:Intellect}, they took Wren back to where she was born. Why home, of all places?
opener: Somewhere warm. I'd settle for a warm supper. Eat.

riddle.q: What has to be broken before you can use it?

callback: Corin was held a morning's walk from his own mill. Wren was told she was going home first.
weekQuestion: What do they need Wren for?
meaningQuestion: *"Then they stopped being ours."* Whose were they, and what took them?

pull: **What does anyone need a child for, once? The Blackglass: half a day up the black road, the place Meira marked.**
forkA: The manners were real.
forkB: The manners are the trick.

leads.place: the well, and the board of chips

actions.verb: crouch by the board and wait
watch the well from across the street

leads.clueText: At the well a boy holds his chip out low and quick, then shoves it back into his shirt before you have looked at it properly.
leads.lateLine: You almost give up. Then, at the last of the light, there it is.

leads.place: the empty cart at the foot of the black road

actions.verb: climb up and look over the boards
go over the cart end to end

leads.clueText: In the bed of the empty cart a sheepskin is spread over the boards, and a blanket is folded at one end like a pillow.
leads.lateLine: You almost give up. Then, at the last of the light, there it is.

leads.place: the street, where every door shut

actions.verb: walk the street with your eyes on the ground
pick out what is caught between the stones

leads.clueText: Caught between the stones down the middle of the street are scraps of sacking. It is the kind men tie over hooves to quiet them on a night road.
leads.lateLine: You almost give up. Then, at the last of the light, there it is.

nudge: {friend:Charm}, why would men taking a child bother with good manners?
opener: Eat first. Then think. It goes better in that order.

riddle.q: What has an eye but cannot see?
riddle.quip: Sharp little thing. Sharper than a polite man.

callback: Tamsin and Corin each came home with one cut palm, bound clean. Wren's taker said they'd only need her the once.
weekQuestion: What do they need Wren for?
meaningQuestion: *"Remember that, when you hear where else we stood."* Where else might they have stood?

pull: **They rode straight past the one thing Meira marked. So what are they riding to? On, into the black ridges.**
forkA: The children were chosen for their place.
forkB: The places were chosen for the children.

leads.place: where the shepherds' path meets the glass

actions.verb: look at where the path gives out
walk the edge of the glass

leads.clueText: Where the shepherds' path meets the glass, a row of old stones lies across it, sunk deep in the turf. The path stops dead at the row.
leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

leads.place: the housing beside the mark

actions.verb: run a finger round its carving
look it over before you step away

leads.clueText: The glass round the housing is dull with fine dust. The only marks in it are the ones your own hand just made.
leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

leads.place: the far edge, where the glass is cracked

actions.verb: look back the way you came
climb onto the highest lip of glass

leads.clueText: From the far edge you can see all the way down the black road to Ashcombe's roofs, and the well in the middle of them.
leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

nudge: {friend:Intellect}, why would a scholar write down a number she doubted?
opener: Mind your hands on that glass, all of you.

riddle.q: Black when you buy it, red when you burn it, grey when you throw it away. What is it?
riddle.quip: Charcoal's cheaper than glass. Kinder to knees.

callback: At the Widow's Tooth a man lay in the bracken watching the rock. Here the riders went past this one without slowing.
weekQuestion: What do they need Wren for?
meaningQuestion: *"He only never told us the price."* The price of what?

pull: **She is alive, and she is thinking. The hut, at first light.**
forkA: The chips are for us.
forkB: The chips are for herself.

leads.place: the rises along the riders' trail

actions.verb: look back down the trail from the last rise
run the trail back to the first chip

leads.clueText: Each chip lay on bare rock at the top of a rise, never down in the ash where it would sink. Coming up behind, you see each one glint before you reach it.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

leads.place: the bone-white trees along the trail

actions.verb: set each chip beside what stood near it
look round from where each one lay

leads.clueText: Each chip lay a few paces from a dead tree, the tallest one in sight. Stand at one tree, and you can see the next.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

leads.place: the three chips in your hand

actions.verb: turn each one over in the light
lay them out side by side

leads.clueText: Turn the chips over. One has a single short scratch on its back, one has two, and one has three.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

nudge: {friend:Agility}, you followed Wren's chips up the ridges. Left for us, or for herself?
opener: She's leaving chips on the trail. Clever girl.

riddle.q: What follows you all day and vanishes at dark?
riddle.quip: Long ones on a ridge at dusk.

callback: Tamsin wasn't asleep; she was counting. Wren is dropping her chips, one by one, on their trail.
weekQuestion: What do they need Wren for?
meaningQuestion: *"We locked with what we are."* What are they?

pull: **A step, now, and no more. If they could see you, can you see them? The cairn on the highest ridge, before the light goes.**
forkA: They left her bed as a message.
forkB: They left it in a hurry.

leads.place: low on the doorframe

actions.verb: run a thumbnail along the letters
look at how each letter was made

leads.clueText: Each stroke of the name has been cut twice, the second pass deeper than the first.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

leads.place: the spring below the hut

actions.verb: get down to the water fast
look over the ground by the spring

leads.clueText: By the spring a water skin lies in the grass, half full. Its stopper is a pace away.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

leads.place: the wall beside the pallet

actions.verb: sit on the pallet and look round
look at what is kept by the bed

leads.clueText: Along the wall by the pallet, small things are set out in a row: a twist of grey wool, a white pebble, a hen's feather. At one end there is a gap, and the dust there is clean.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

nudge: {friend:Craft}, what tool cuts letters like that into wood?

riddle.q: What goes through a door but never goes in or out?
riddle.quip: Doors keep secrets better than people.

weekQuestion: What do they need Wren for?
meaningQuestion: *"That is why kingdoms fear them."* Why would a kingdom fear a family?

pull: **Whatever happens under that hill has started. Into the Kiln, tonight.**

leads.lateLine: You almost give up. Then, at the last of the light, there it is.

weekQuestion: What do they need Wren for?
meaningQuestion: *"We never dug him a grave."* Why not?

pull:
*Already with us.* Joss is not waiting to be taken.

forkA: He had help in the room.

actions.verb: go a few steps in, without a lamp

leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

actions.verb: pace it out from the passage

riddle.q: What can you break without ever touching it?

weekQuestion: What do they need Joss for?

pull: **Four armed men for one small box, riding away from the boy. What is in it? Reedham, by noon tomorrow.**

leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

actions.verb: sit down in the water with them

leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

leads.clueText: Their ruts keep to the open road the whole way, past every shepherd's hut. A sheep-path along the ridge would have hidden them from all of it.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

nudge: {friend:Intellect}, who scrapes a face off a coin?

weekQuestion: What do they need Joss for?
meaningQuestion: *"The fifth had no element at all."* What could it be, if it is not earth, wind, water or fire?

pull:
Back on the shingle, beside the place her skiff was lying, there are keel-marks that are not hers. Fresh ones.

**Someone has been rowing out to the drowned village by night. Old Reedham, at the shallow end, tomorrow.**
forkA: They're waiting for the right night.
forkB: They're waiting for the right child.

leads.place: the fisherman on the shingle

actions.verb: help him with his nets and listen

actions.verb: walk the lane up from the shingle

leads.clueText: Small dark spots of lamp-oil stain the stones of the lane, a pace apart. They go up to her door and back, and to no other door.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

actions.verb: climb up to the sill from the skiff

leads.clueText: On the tower's lowest sill, on the side facing Reedham, the weed is scraped away in a patch the size of a seat. From there you can see her window.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

nudge: {friend:Craft}, what does a skiff tell you about its owner?
opener: A lamp in a window at noon. Somebody has kept it lit for eight nights.

riddle.q: What gets wetter the more it dries?

callback: In Ashcombe a baby born when the moon goes out is given a chip of black glass. In Reedham every window is lit for one.
weekQuestion: What do they need Joss for?
meaningQuestion: *"So does anyone born in its dark."* What does a child born in the dark have in common with what fell?

pull: **A warning against what? The reed island, a mile out: the only place on this lake a boat can put in unseen.**
forkA: 'Moon-blood' just means the marked children.

actions.verb: look along the windows in the low light

leads.lateLine: You almost give up. Then, at the last of the light, there it is.

actions.verb: go back through them, page by page

riddle.q: What is full of holes but still holds water?

weekQuestion: What do they need Joss for?
meaningQuestion: *"Moon-blood woke it once."* What did it wake, and when?

pull: **Why would anyone keep watch on an empty tower? After that lamp, tonight, in their own boat.**

actions.verb: feel under the thwart

leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

nudge: {friend:Aim}, they moved Joss by water once. Would they risk the lake again?
opener: Pale curls of whittled wood. Somebody's still carving.

riddle.q: What floats when empty and sinks when full?
riddle.quip: Yours is on loan. I'd return it.

callback: At the Widow's Tooth a little carved horse was left behind. Today, in their boat, a little carved hull was thrown away.
weekQuestion: What do they need Joss for?
meaningQuestion: *"Pray no one ever learns it is also a door."* A door to what, and who would want it opened?

pull: **Down the stair, into the boat you took from them, and after that sound. Now.**

riddle.q: What can you hear but never touch?

weekQuestion: What do they need Joss for?
meaningQuestion: *"We never asked what that would make them."* What has it made them?

pull:
At dusk the heartbeat comes again. It is louder than it was at dawn.

forkA: The fifth is a Stone like the others.

weekQuestion: What will it take for the fifth to end this?

weekQuestion: What will it take for the fifth to end this?
meaningQuestion: *"None of us gave to the fifth."* Why give to four and not to the fifth?

riddle.q: What turns but never leaves its post?

callback: On the road, when the beat stopped, the dogs stopped where they stood. These soldiers stopped mid-stride, and never started again.
weekQuestion: What will it take for the fifth to end this?
meaningQuestion: *"We could not bring ourselves to break them."* Why not?

actions.verb: slip round to its back wall

leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

nudge: {friend:Intellect}, what ends when the count ends?
opener: One chalk stroke each dusk. Somebody's counting.

riddle.q: What burns shorter every night but is never cut?

callback: At Reedham they kept Joss eight nights, waiting for something. Here they strike off one night every dusk.
weekQuestion: What will it take for the fifth to end this?
meaningQuestion: *"Where we could watch it, and watch him."* Why keep the two so close?

pull: **The watch has changed. It is dark enough. Into the wall, tonight.**
forkA: The room was built to hide the fifth.

actions.verb: lean out over the parapet

opener: A slit window, a hidden room, a night nobody heard you.

riddle.quip: A room hollowed out of a wall is one.

callback: Every map before tonight was read out loud. Tonight it went hand to hand, and nobody heard.
weekQuestion: What will it take for the fifth to end this?
meaningQuestion: *"Where he fell, under the dark moon, the five were joined."* Why there, and why that night?

pull: **The hall is sealed, and the Seekers left a way in, somewhere. The arrow points down: the defenders' barracks, under the wall.**
forkA: They think the light was nothing.
forkB: They know someone's in the wall.

actions.verb: watch the lanterns from the slit

leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

actions.verb: watch the board from the slit at dusk

actions.verb: hold a hand inside and feel the stone

leads.clueText: The back of the stone niche is blackened in one small round patch, the way a candle marks stone over years. The niche faces the inner wall, away from the slit.
leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

opener: Quiet's good in a hole in a wall. I'll take it.

riddle.q: What can fill a room and take no space?

callback: At dusk you crossed the wall and nobody heard. By the end of the night a watchman was looking straight at your window.
weekQuestion: What will the fifth do in his hall?

pull: **They are not coming for you. They are going to him. And wherever the Seekers' way in begins, it begins at his walls. The great square, after dark.**
forkA: They go up to the hall to answer a call.
forkB: They go up to guard it.

leads.place: where the spears once stood

actions.verb: look at the dust under the racks

leads.clueText: The spear-racks along the wall are empty, and the dust under every one is swept clean in the same short arc.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

leads.place: the stair up to the street

actions.verb: climb to the top step and listen

leads.clueText: When the heartbeat comes, you hear iron move all over the city at once: one scrape of a foot from every street, then quiet.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

actions.verb: look over the board and the pot

leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

nudge: {friend:Agility}, the dead passed us by on their way up. Called, or on guard?
place: The barracks under the wall (Five nights)
opener: The dead move when nobody watches, and they passed you by. Sit down a minute.

riddle.q: What can you hold but never see, and the more you hold it the less you speak?

callback: Last week you couldn't be sure a helm had turned toward you. Today one stood in your doorway and looked at the fallen stone instead.
weekQuestion: What will the fifth do in his hall?
meaningQuestion: *"That is how we found the shards."* How could a mark help anyone find one?

pull: **He is on the other side of this wall. Inside, on the night the moon goes dark, with the fifth: that is the whole plan now. The cracked hill behind the hall.**
forkA: There is no way in at the front.

actions.verb: slip along the wall to the doors

leads.clueText: At the foot of the great doors, dust has drifted against the seam in one smooth bank, from post to post. Nothing has crossed it.

actions.verb: pick out what is stacked by their fire

leads.clueText: By the Order's fire the new men's packs are stacked in a row. On top of each lies a folded robe, brushed clean of the road.
leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

actions.verb: feel the stone, hand over hand

leads.lateLine: It takes you until full dark, but you find it.

nudge: {friend:Intellect}, where would the Seekers have left a door?
opener: The hall's warm from within. More faithful arriving. What's missing is a door.

riddle.q: What is warm in the cold but has no fire?

callback: The soldiers are three streets nearer the hall. Round the Order's fire there are twice as many as before.
weekQuestion: What will the fifth do in his hall?
meaningQuestion: *"None of us could bear to lift him."* What kept them from lifting him?

forkA: The rock waits for the dark moon.
forkB: The rock will open for us now.

actions.verb: go in sideways, lamp first

leads.clueText: Past where the soldier stood, the grit on the crack's floor lies smooth and untouched. Your boots are the first marks in it.

actions.verb: drag the broken armour aside

leads.clueText: The rock where it stood is worn into two shallow hollows, one for each foot. It stood on that one spot, facing out, for a very long time.
leads.lateLine: You almost give up. Then, at the last of the light, there it is.

actions.verb: squeeze on to the very end
keep everyone quiet, and listen

leads.clueText: Put your ear to the blank rock. When the heartbeat comes, it is louder here than anywhere else in the crack.
leads.lateLine: You almost give up. Then, at the last of the light, there it is.

nudge: {friend:Craft}, nobody has walked that crack before us. Why keep a soldier at it?
place: The hill behind the hall (Three nights)
opener: That hill was steeper than it looked. Sit.

riddle.q: What changes shape but is never touched?

callback: Upriver, a dog on a chain kept the hidden path. Today a soldier stood in the crack with its back to the hall.
weekQuestion: What will the fifth do in his hall?
meaningQuestion: *"Forgive us for leaving it at all."* Why would leaving a way in need forgiving?

pull: **You have the hour. One piece is left, and the Seekers' way ends at a blank rock with this same moon beside it. Tomorrow is the last day.**
forkA: The Seekers chose the dark moon.
forkB: The dark moon came by chance.

leads.place: the sky-watchers' wall, row by row

actions.verb: measure the space between the moons
follow one row all the way round

leads.clueText: Lay a finger between any two moons, on any row. The space is the same every time, year on year, round the whole room.
leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

leads.place: the floor of the round room

actions.verb: gather up what lies on the floor
read the scratches by daylight

leads.clueText: On the floor lie the sky-watchers' slates, scratched with long sums. Many are crossed through and begun again.
leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

leads.place: where the rows stop

actions.verb: climb the ledges to the last rows
run a thumb along the last cuts

leads.clueText: In the last rows before they stop, every moon is cut to the right depth, but the edges are rough, as if made in a hurry. Not one night is missing.
leads.lateLine: You go over the same ground twice before you see it.

nudge: {friend:Intellect}, the sky-watchers' record stops on one night. Why that night?
opener: Two nights. Eat while there's something to eat.

riddle.q: What is taken every night and returned at dawn?

callback: The Order's board has counted down for generations. The sky-watchers' wall, counted forward, lands on the same night.
weekQuestion: What will the fifth do in his hall?
meaningQuestion: *"Be there when it does."* Be there to do what?

pull: **Tomorrow night, when the moon goes dark: through the Seekers' door, into his hall, with the fifth in your hands.**
forkA: We open the rock tomorrow night.
forkB: The door is not ours to open tomorrow.

leads.place: the street below the crack

actions.verb: watch the street from the crack's mouth
count the ranks as they climb

leads.clueText: From the crack's mouth you can see the whole street climbing toward you. Every helm in it is turned to the hall, not one to the hill.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

leads.place: the foot of the blank rock

actions.verb: look at how the grit lies
get down low with the lamp

leads.clueText: At the foot of the blank rock, the old grit on your side lies swept flat in a smooth quarter-circle. Its point is at the rock's left edge.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

leads.place: the streets you crossed this morning

actions.verb: look back down the hill from the crack
go back the long way, street by street

leads.clueText: The crossroads, the gate-tower, the street under the wall: every place where a soldier stood is empty now. Only the pale marks of their boots are left.
leads.lateLine: By the time you find it, the fire is the only light left.

nudge: {friend:Intellect}, not one of the dead turned its head. What do they know that we don't?
place: The crack in the hill (One night)
opener: Last night of the count. Eat what you like.

riddle.q: What gets better when you share it and worse when you keep it?

callback: Six nights ago you had a hidden room. Tonight you have one stroke left.
weekQuestion: What will the fifth do in his hall?
meaningQuestion: *"Finish what we could not."* What did the Seekers leave unfinished?
